Design a URL Shortener (TinyURL) & Design a Distributed Rate Limiter
Design a Social Media News Feed (Twitter/Instagram fan-out-on-write vs. hybrid fan-out-on-read)
Design a Real-Time Chat System (WhatsApp/Slack WebSockets, presence, message ordering)
Design a Notification Service, Web Crawler, Payment System (idempotency & ledger), and Proximity/Ride-Sharing (QuadTree/Geohash)

resources.title: System Design Primer — System Design Interview Solutions
ByteByteGo — How to Ace System Design Interviews

exercises: Whiteboard complete 45-minute designs (with QPS/storage math, schema, APIs, and component diagram) for: (1) TinyURL, (2) Twitter News Feed, (3) WhatsApp Chat, and (4) Payment Gateway.
interviewQuestions: In a Twitter/Instagram News Feed, why does pure fan-out-on-write fail for users with 50 million followers, and how does a hybrid push/pull model solve it?
How do you guarantee zero duplicate charges and exact ledger reconciliation in a distributed Payment System?
topics.interviewRelevance: Directly decides leveling (SDE-1 vs. SDE-2 vs. Senior SDE) in technical loops.
topics.completionCriteria: Can drive a 45-minute HLD discussion unprompted, covering capacity math, APIs, data model, scaling, and failure modes.

phases.title: Phase 7: Software Engineering Ecosystem
phases.subtitle: Cloud architecture, Docker, Kubernetes, CI/CD, IaC, Security engineering, and SRE observability
phases.summary: Consolidates Cloud, DevOps & Infrastructure (Section 3), Security Engineering & Authentication (Section 11), and Testing, Reliability & Observability (Section 14) into the production engineering ecosystem.
phases.whyThisOrder: Once you understand how distributed systems are designed (Phase 6), Phase 7 teaches how they are deployed, containerized, secured, monitored, and operated in cloud production environments.

topics.title: Cloud Computing, Compute, Storage & Cloud Networking
topics.summary: Covers IaaS/PaaS/SaaS, regions/AZs, RTO/RPO disaster recovery, VPC networking, IAM least privilege, compute choices (EC2, ECS/Fargate, EKS, Lambda), and managed storage (S3, EBS, EFS, RDS, DynamoDB, ElastiCache).
topics.whyImportant: Modern backend systems run on cloud primitives; interviews test practical trade-offs like Serverless vs. Containers and S3 vs. EBS.

subtopics.name: Cloud fundamentals: Regions, Availability Zones, High Availability vs. Disaster Recovery (RTO & RPO), IaaS/PaaS/SaaS
Compute decisions: EC2 vs. ECS/Fargate vs. EKS vs. AWS Lambda (triggers, cold starts, concurrency, idempotency)
Storage decisions: EBS vs. EFS vs. S3 (versioning, lifecycle, presigned URLs), RDS/Aurora failover, DynamoDB, ElastiCache
Cloud Networking & Identity: VPC, public/private subnets, NAT/IGW, Security Groups vs. NACLs, IAM roles & temporary credentials
Cost & Capacity: Capacity planning (throughput/p95), Reserved vs. On-Demand vs. Spot, multi-region drills

resources.title: ByteByteGo System Design 101 — Cloud & Infrastructure Guides

exercises: Diagram a production multi-AZ VPC architecture with public ALB/NAT subnets, private app subnets, and isolated RDS database subnets.
interviewQuestions: When would you choose AWS Lambda over ECS/Kubernetes, and when do Lambda cold starts or cost models make containers better?
How do S3 Presigned URLs allow clients to upload large media files directly to object storage without bottlenecking your API servers?
topics.interviewRelevance: Essential for cloud-native backend and system design discussions.
topics.completionCriteria: Can compare cloud compute/storage options and design secure VPC/IAM topologies.

topics.title: Docker Containerization & Kubernetes Orchestration
topics.summary: Covers Docker images, layers, multi-stage builds, container security/isolation, and Kubernetes architecture (Pods, Deployments, Services, Ingress, ConfigMaps/Secrets, Probes, HPA, and troubleshooting).
topics.whyImportant: Containers and Kubernetes are the industry standard for packaging and scaling backend services.

subtopics.name: Docker: Images, layers, registries, Dockerfiles, multi-stage builds, build caching, and non-root container security
Container networking, volumes, cgroups resource limits, and namespace isolation
Kubernetes Core: Pods, Deployments, ReplicaSets, Services, Ingress, ConfigMaps, Secrets, Namespaces, and RBAC
Kubernetes Operations: Liveness/Readiness/Startup probes, resource requests/limits, HPA, StatefulSets, and debugging CrashLoopBackOff

exercises: Write a multi-stage Dockerfile for a backend API that runs as a non-root user and reduces image size by >60%.
Write Kubernetes Deployment, Service, and HPA manifests with readiness and liveness probes.
interviewQuestions: What is the difference between a Kubernetes Liveness Probe and a Readiness Probe, and what happens if a Readiness Probe fails?
How would you debug a Pod stuck in `CrashLoopBackOff` or `Pending` state?
topics.interviewRelevance: Frequently asked in backend, platform, and microservices interviews.
topics.completionCriteria: Can write optimized multi-stage Dockerfiles and troubleshoot Kubernetes Pod/Deployment lifecycles.

topics.title: CI/CD Release Engineering & Infrastructure as Code (IaC)
topics.summary: Covers automated build/test/deploy pipelines, GitHub Actions, safe deployment strategies (Blue-Green, Canary, Rolling, Feature Flags), backward-compatible DB migrations, and Terraform/CDK IaC.
topics.whyImportant: Shipping code safely without downtime requires automated quality gates, progressive rollouts, and reproducible infrastructure.

subtopics.name: CI/CD pipelines, quality gates, and GitHub Actions (workflows, runners, permissions, artifacts)
Zero-downtime releases: Blue-Green, Canary, Rolling deployments, Feature Flags, and safe backward-compatible DB migrations
Infrastructure as Code (IaC): Terraform vs. CloudFormation/CDK, remote state locking, drift detection, secrets handling
Supply-chain security, dependency scanning, and artifact provenance

resources.title: ByteByteGo System Design 101 — CI/CD & Deployment Strategies

exercises: Create a GitHub Actions workflow that runs lint, unit tests, builds a container image, and deploys on main branch push.
interviewQuestions: How do you perform a zero-downtime database schema migration (such as renaming a column) while old and new service versions run simultaneously (Expand-and-Contract pattern)?
Compare Blue-Green deployment vs. Canary deployment vs. Feature Flags.
topics.interviewRelevance: Zero-downtime deployment and backward-compatible schema migrations are classic senior SDE questions.
topics.completionCriteria: Can design CI/CD pipelines and explain Expand-and-Contract database migrations and Canary rollouts.

topics.title: Security Engineering, AuthN/AuthZ & Cryptography
topics.summary: Covers Authentication vs. Authorization, OAuth 2.0 + PKCE, OIDC, JWTs, Sessions/Cookies, RBAC/ABAC, OWASP Top 10 (SQLi, XSS, CSRF, SSRF, BOLA/IDOR), TLS/mTLS, and password/data encryption.
topics.whyImportant: Security vulnerabilities can compromise an entire company; every backend engineer must know how to authenticate requests and prevent OWASP Top 10 attacks.

subtopics.name: AuthN & AuthZ: Sessions/Cookies (HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite) vs. JWTs (claims, signature, rotation), OAuth 2.0 (Auth Code + PKCE), OIDC, SSO/MFA/Passkeys
Access Control: RBAC vs. ABAC, Broken Object-Level Authorization (BOLA/IDOR), and service-to-service workload identity
Application Security & OWASP Top 10: SQL/NoSQL Injection, XSS & CSP, CSRF, SSRF, CORS, rate limiting, and safe deserialization
Cryptography & Data Protection: TLS/mTLS handshake, symmetric vs. asymmetric encryption, envelope encryption, KMS, password hashing (Argon2/bcrypt + salt)
Threat modeling (STRIDE), least privilege, SAST/DAST/SCA, and tamper-evident security audit logs

exercises: Audit a sample REST API for SQL Injection, IDOR/BOLA, XSS, and insecure JWT storage, and patch each vulnerability.
interviewQuestions: Compare stateful session cookies vs. stateless JWTs: how do you handle immediate token revocation when a user logs out or is compromised?
Explain how OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code flow with PKCE works and how OIDC builds identity on top of OAuth 2.0.
topics.interviewRelevance: JWT vs. Sessions, OAuth 2.0, TLS, and SQLi/XSS/CSRF are asked in almost every backend and system design loop.
topics.completionCriteria: Can design secure AuthN/AuthZ flows, explain TLS & Argon2/bcrypt, and mitigate OWASP Top 10 vulnerabilities.

topics.title: Observability, Performance Optimization & Reliability (SRE)
topics.summary: Covers the 3 pillars of observability (Structured Logs, Metrics, Distributed Tracing with OpenTelemetry), RED/USE methods, SLIs/SLOs/SLAs, error budgets, resilience patterns (retries with jitter, backpressure, circuit breakers), load testing, and incident response.
topics.whyImportant: Designing reliable systems requires knowing how to measure p99 latency, correlate traces across services, and prevent retry storms during outages.

subtopics.name: Three Pillars of Observability: Structured Logging (correlation IDs), Metrics (cardinality, histograms), and Distributed Tracing (OpenTelemetry spans)
Monitoring methodologies: RED (Rate, Errors, Duration), USE (Utilization, Saturation, Errors), and burn-rate alerting
SRE & Resilience: SLIs, SLOs, SLAs, Error Budgets, Exponential Backoff with Jitter, Circuit Breakers, Bulkheads, Graceful Degradation
Performance Engineering: Load vs. Stress vs. Soak vs. Spike testing, p50/p95/p99 tail latency, CPU/memory/DB query profiling
Incident Excellence: Triage, mitigation, rollback, root-cause analysis, and blameless postmortems

exercises: Instrument a two-service HTTP application with correlation IDs, structured JSON logs, and latency histograms, and write an exponential backoff + jitter retry client.
interviewQuestions: Why must exponential backoff retries always include random jitter during a partial downstream outage?
What is the difference between an SLI, an SLO, and an SLA, and why is average latency a dangerous metric compared to p95/p99?
topics.interviewRelevance: Heavily tested in System Design, Backend, and Operational Excellence / SRE rounds.
topics.completionCriteria: Can define SLIs/SLOs, instrument logs/metrics/traces, and prevent cascading failures with jittered retries and circuit breakers.

phases.title: Phase 8: Interview Preparation & Execution
phases.subtitle: DSA pattern mastery, interview communication, behavioral STAR stories, resume prep, and revision plans
phases.summary: Transforms raw technical knowledge from Phases 1–7 into interview performance: pattern recognition under time pressure, structured communication, behavioral leadership stories, resume impact, and timed mock execution.
phases.whyThisOrder: Placed as the capstone phase so candidates synthesize their coding, LLD, HLD, and production engineering skills into timed, high-signal interview delivery.

topics.title: Coding Interview Strategy & 15 Core DSA Practice Patterns
topics.originalSection: 9. Problem-solving and Coding / Interview Readiness Assessment
topics.summary: Maps coding prompts to the 15 recurring DSA patterns (Two Pointers, Sliding Window, Fast/Slow Pointers, Merge Intervals, Cyclic Sort, Monotonic Stack, Top-K Heap, Tree BFS/DFS, Graph Topo Sort/Union-Find, Binary Search on Answer, Backtracking, and 1D/2D DP).
topics.whyImportant: In a 45-minute coding round, recognizing the underlying pattern in 2–3 minutes leaves 35+ minutes for clean implementation, dry-running, and complexity analysis.

subtopics.name: Pattern recognition matrix: mapping problem constraints (N <= 20 vs. N <= 10^5) to target time complexity
45-Minute Coding Protocol: Clarify constraints (3m) -> Approach & complexity (5m) -> Clean code (25m) -> Dry run & edge cases (7m)
Curated 75 / 150 problem sheet mastery across all 15 patterns without hints

resources.title: Tech Interview Handbook — Grind 75 & Coding Interview Rubric

exercises: Complete 5 timed 45-minute coding sessions solving two unseen Medium/Hard problems back-to-back while speaking your thought process aloud.
interviewQuestions: If input size N = 10^5, which time complexities are acceptable (O(N), O(N log N)) and why will O(N^2) time out?
What edge cases should you always test before telling the interviewer your code is complete?
topics.interviewRelevance: Directly governs pass rates in OA, phone screen, and onsite coding rounds.
topics.completionCriteria: Can solve Medium DSA problems in <25 minutes while articulating invariants, edge cases, and exact complexity.

topics.title: Technical Communication, Mock Interviews & Design Rubrics
topics.summary: Covers how interviewers score rubrics across Coding, LLD, and HLD rounds, how to drive trade-off discussions, handle hints gracefully, and apply the repository's 6-point Interview Readiness Assessment.
topics.whyImportant: Many strong engineers fail interviews due to silent coding, jumping into implementation before clarifying scope, or failing to defend trade-offs.

subtopics.name: Repository 6-Point Interview Readiness Self-Assessment (0–4 scale: aim for 3+ on all P0 topics)
Driving LLD & HLD interviews: pacing the 45-minute clock, proposing trade-offs proactively, and checking in with the interviewer
Mock interview feedback loop: recording and auditing communication clarity, hint reception, and bug discovery

exercises: Complete 3 full mock interviews (1 DSA, 1 LLD, 1 HLD) and score yourself against the 6-point Readiness Rubric.
interviewQuestions: How do you recover in an interview when your initial approach hits a dead end or the interviewer points out a flaw?
How do you structure a 2-minute explanation of your most complex past architecture project?
topics.interviewRelevance: Determines hiring committee calibration and leveling decisions.
topics.completionCriteria: Achieves Level 3+ ('Explain and apply unaided') across all Must-Learn (P0) topics in the Readiness Assessment.

topics.title: Behavioral Interviews (STAR Method), Leadership & Resume Prep
topics.summary: Covers engineering resume optimization (impact-first XYZ bullets), building a 6–8 story matrix using the STAR framework (Situation, Task, Action, Result), conflict resolution, failure/postmortem stories, and company-specific values.
topics.whyImportant: Behavioral and leadership rounds carry veto power at top tech companies and often decide between adjacent levels (e.g., L4 vs. L5).

subtopics.name: Engineering Resume optimization: Action + Metric + Technical Context (XYZ formula) and ATS clarity
STAR Story Matrix: Ownership, Technical Disagreement, Tight Deadline, Production Incident/Failure, Mentorship, Ambiguity
Company-specific preparation: Amazon Leadership Principles, Google Googleyness, Meta Engineering Execution

resources.title: Tech Interview Handbook — Resume & Behavioral Interview Guide

exercises: Write out 6 distinct STAR stories from your projects/experience, each with quantifiable outcomes and a 'What I learned' reflection.
interviewQuestions: Tell me about a time you disagreed with a senior engineer or manager on a technical design. How did you resolve it?
Tell me about a production bug or project failure you owned, how you mitigated it, and what systemic fix you put in place.
topics.interviewRelevance: Tested in hiring manager screens and dedicated behavioral / bar-raiser rounds.
topics.completionCriteria: Has a polished 1-page resume and 6 rehearsed STAR stories adaptable to any behavioral prompt.

topics.title: Structured Interview Revision Plans (4-Week, 8-Week & 12-Week)
topics.summary: Provides actionable week-by-week revision schedules (4-week sprint for experienced engineers, 8-week balanced plan, and 12-week beginner-to-advanced plan) plus final-week cheatsheets.
topics.whyImportant: Spaced repetition prevents forgetting Phase 2 DSA patterns while studying Phase 6–7 System Design and Cloud topics.

subtopics.name: 12-Week Comprehensive Track (Beginner to SDE-1/SDE-2)
8-Week Accelerated Track (Intermediate SDE Refresher)
4-Week High-Yield Sprint (P0 Must-Learn Topics + Daily Timed Drills)

exercises: Select your target timeline (4, 8, or 12 weeks) and bookmark your weekly topic targets in the Interactive Learning Dashboard.
interviewQuestions: Self-check: Can you explain every P0 topic in Phases 1–7 in under 2 minutes without notes?
topics.interviewRelevance: Keeps preparation consistent and measurable right up to interview day.
topics.completionCriteria: Completed a full revision cycle across all P0 topics with >85% readiness score.

phases.title: Optional Specialization: Agentic AI, LLM Engineering & AI System Design
phases.subtitle: LLMs, RAG, prompt/tool engineering, multi-agent orchestration, evaluation, and AI system design
phases.summary: Preserves 100% of the original repository's Section 1 ('Agentic AI, LLM Engineering, and AI System Design') plus the LLM Security (Section 11) and LLM Evaluation (Section 14) checklists, repositioned from Section 1 to an advanced post-core specialization track so beginners are never overwhelmed early.
phases.whyThisOrder: Building production RAG pipelines and multi-agent architectures requires solid foundations in APIs, databases/vector indexes, distributed caching, queues, security, and observability from Phases 1–7.

topics.title: LLM Fundamentals, Prompt Engineering & RAG Architectures
topics.originalSection: 1. Agentic AI, LLM Engineering, and AI System Design
topics.summary: Covers Transformer/token fundamentals, model selection, structured JSON schema outputs, function/tool calling, embeddings, vector indexes (HNSW, IVF), chunking, hybrid BM25 + dense retrieval, reranking, and RAG evaluation.
topics.whyImportant: Essential for AI Engineer, Applied LLM, and modern backend SDE roles building AI-powered features.

subtopics.name: LLM Fundamentals: Transformers, attention, tokens/context windows, temperature/top-p, closed vs. open-weight, Prompting vs. RAG vs. Fine-tuning
Prompt Engineering & Structured Outputs: system/user/tool priority, JSON Schema validation, function/tool calling, handling refusals & long context
RAG Pipelines: chunking (fixed/semantic/hierarchical), embeddings, Vector DBs (HNSW, IVF), hybrid search (BM25 + dense), reranking, multi-tenant ACL filtering
RAG Evaluation: recall@k, precision@k, MRR, nDCG, faithfulness, groundedness, and citations

resources.title: Original Repository — Agentic AI, LLM Engineering & AI System Design Checklist

exercises: Build a RAG pipeline with semantic chunking, hybrid search, source citations, and a golden evaluation dataset measuring recall@5 and faithfulness.
interviewQuestions: How do you decide between Long-Context Prompting, Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), and Fine-Tuning for a domain question-answering system?
Why does combining sparse keyword search (BM25) with dense vector embeddings (Hybrid Search + Reranking) outperform vector search alone?
topics.interviewRelevance: Core topic for AI SDE and modern system design rounds.
topics.completionCriteria: Can architect, evaluate, and optimize an ACL-aware production RAG pipeline.

topics.title: Agentic Workflows, Multi-Agent Systems, Safety & AI System Design
topics.summary: Covers core agent loops (ReAct), workflows vs. autonomous agents, LangGraph/checkpointing, MCP & tool contracts, memory management, multi-agent coordination, LLM-as-judge evaluation, prompt injection defense, and agentic system design case studies.
topics.whyImportant: Prepares engineers for cutting-edge Agentic AI system design interviews, covering reliability, cost/latency budgets, and safety guardrails.

subtopics.name: Agent Fundamentals: observe-decide-act loop, ReAct, deterministic workflows vs. autonomous agents, human-in-the-loop approvals, turn budgets
Orchestration & State: LangGraph state graphs, checkpointing, durable execution, short-term vs. episodic/semantic memory, context compaction
Tool Use & Multi-Agent Systems: MCP protocol, idempotent tools, parallel tool execution, supervisor/worker vs. single-agent trade-offs
Evaluation, Reliability & Security: trajectory tests, LLM-as-judge calibration, prompt/response caching, token cost/p95 latency budgets, prompt injection & sandboxing
Agentic System Design Practice: code-review agent, customer-support agent with handoff, document research agent, incident-response assistant

resources.title: Original Repository — Agentic System Design Interview Practice

exercises: Build a stateful tool-calling agent with schema validation, persistent checkpointing, retry backoff, and human approval gates for write actions.
interviewQuestions: When should you build a deterministic pipeline/workflow instead of an autonomous LLM agent, and how do you enforce safety on write/side-effect tools?
How do you defend an agent with database/email tool access against indirect prompt injection embedded in untrusted documents?
topics.interviewRelevance: Directly targets Agentic AI and LLM System Design interview loops.
topics.completionCriteria: Can whiteboard an end-to-end agentic architecture with token/latency math, evaluation rubrics, and security boundaries.
